text:
Maya (Partnerships): Quick sync: we're proposing to deprecate SDK auth header v1 (X-Redwood-Key) in favor of Authorization: Bearer + signed key (v2). This touches marketplace vendors and HW partners that ship pinned SDKs. Proposing a 6-month sunset + partner grace options. Need partner coordination plan. Thoughts?
Omar (Platform): 6 months is reasonable generally. Question: do we have a compatibility shim for firmware/embedded partners? Some HW partners push SDKs into device images.
Sofia (Eng): We can ship a runtime proxy/shim that translates `X-Redwood-Key` -> `Authorization` behind a feature flag for a limited time (9 months-ish). It adds maintenance burden but buys partners time.
Luca (SDKs): Suggest staged rollout: 1) opt-in v2 in SDKs within 2 weeks, 2) default v2 in SDKs in ~3 months, 3) hard cut at 6 months. We'll provide migration script, sample code, and a dockerized test harness. I'll open PR.
Ana (Acme): FWIW Acme's firmware refresh cadence is quarterly. A 6-month sunset feels tight; asks for 9-12 months or a marketplace "vendor grace" so devices in the field aren't bricked.
Maya (Partnerships): Noted. We can offer partner-specific grace periods via the marketplace listing for certified vendors, but that needs legal/ops sign-off. Also we must coordinate customer-facing comms + any joint announcement windows.
release-bot: Reminder: marketplace packaging or API contract changes require a 4-week review cycle. See https://redwood.dev/marketplace-guidelines
Omar (Platform): Two asks: (a) can we keep the legacy endpoint behind a feature flag to limit exposure? (b) what's the rollback plan if migration telemetry shows regression?
Sofia (Eng): Yes, proxy + feature flag is doable. Rollback plan: flip feature flag, enforce temporary rate limit and revert SDK default. We'll add a metric `sdk_auth_migration_failures` and dashboard.
Luca (SDKs): Migration helper (draft): `redwood-sdk migrate-auth --from v1 --to v2 --check` will surface callers still using v1. We'll include sample changelog entries and a migration snippet for common languages.
Ana (Acme): We'll need a signed compatibility statement and a joint FAQ for customers/operators. Can Redwood commit to partner-specific grace if we sign an addendum?
Maya (Partnerships): We can offer a partner addendum granting a grace extension up to +6 months conditionally (telemetry sharing, upgraded support SLA). I'll draft an addendum template.
Luca (SDKs): I'll tag the PR `sdk-auth-v2` and include package pins + migration tests. Ping me for SDK package versions and canary instructions.
Maya (Partnerships): Action items: Maya - draft partner addendum (due 2025-02-10); Luca - PR + migration script (due 2025-02-03); Sofia - proxy flag + metrics (due 2025-01-28); Omar - coordinate marketplace review & docs path (due 2025-01-25); Ana - confirm preferred grace window (ASAP). :thumbsup:
Ana (Acme): Confirming Acme requests a 10-month grace window. I'll escalate with legal/product and update partner timeline by EOD.
Omar (Platform): Recommend we run a 5% traffic canary 3 months before cutoff to detect regressions early and stop sweep if failure rate > 0.5%.
Maya (Partnerships): Agreed. Also scheduling a partner tabletop run two weeks after Luca's PR merges to validate rollback/runbook. I'll send calendar invites to partners and internal owners.
Sofia (Eng): Proxy mapping example for engineers:
```
# proxy mapping (pseudo)
if req.headers.get('X-Redwood-Key'):
  req.headers['Authorization'] = 'Bearer ' + sign(req.headers['X-Redwood-Key'])
```
Luca (SDKs): I'll include CI checks to fail builds that remove v1 without a migration guide.
Maya (Partnerships): Thanks all — keeping this thread as the canonical coordination point. I'll attach the draft addendum here once ready and cc @Ana.
